top_news.title: Trump says Houthis
top_news.summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday (local time) criticised Yemen's Houthi rebels for their escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying the group was "misbehaving very badly". "The Houthis are misbehaving very badly. No good," Trump told reporters when asked what the United States would do about the Houthis. When asked whether the Houthi attacks had increased in connection with the US midterm elections, Trump said, "I don't know how it affects the election. I don't take that into account," he said. "I just know Iran will never have a nuclear weapon...They're never going to have a nuclear weapon. But the Houthis are misbehaving," Trump added. His remarks come amid a series of attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, including incidents involving Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. Trump had earlier said that Washington would consider joining Saudi Arabia in military operations against the Houthis following the latest attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. "We just found out about the recent attack - we'll make a decision," Trump told reporters at the White House on Saturday (local time), adding, "We're going to take a look." Regional diplomatic efforts continued as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Monday held a telephone conversation with his Iraqi counterpart, Fuad Hussein, to discuss developments in the region. According to Al Jazeera, Hussein's Telegram channel said the two ministers exchanged views on the latest regional developments, including the worsening situation in Yemen, where the Houthi militia and Saudi Arabia's armed forces have been trading attacks. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition on Tuesday claimed that it had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi militia towards the Khamis Mushait airbase in Saudi Arabia, as the country faces escalating attacks following a series of deadly strikes on its airports in recent days. In a post on X, the coalition spokesperson, Turki Al-Maliki, said, "Interception and destruction of two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Khamis Mushait." Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence agency had earlier issued an alert asking residents in Khamis Mushait Governorate to remain vigilant over a potential threat.
